headline: Approved consent agenda and discussed Wallingford Works for Housing, REX Development, and a proposed historic train station coalition.
summary: Members heard committee and staff reports on housing education, the Midwood warehouse application, and tax incentives. The Midwood application for three warehouses was denied, and the court upheld that denial. The only vote recorded was approval of the consent agenda.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including adoption of meeting minutes dated October 5, 2026, by unanimous vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner Lombardi made a motion to approve the Consent Agenda. Commissioner McAnneny seconded the motion. Consent Agenda was unanimously approved.

Planning and Zoning Committee 47 
• Mr. Crouch provided an update on the Midwood property application for three warehouses. 48 
The Planning and Zoning Commission denied the application, the developers appealed the 49 
decision, but the denial was subsequently upheld by the court. 50 
• The Commission also discussed the mixed-use floating zone. 51

Housing/Workforce Development/Education Committee 53 
Commissioner Gomes provided an update on Wallingford Works for Housing (WWFH). Noting 54 
that meetings have started to focus on education and awareness surrounding housing issues. 55 
Discussion included the importance of distinguishing affordable housing from subsidized housing 56 
and educating the community about the full spectrum of housing options. 57 
 58 
Chairman Bracale suggested the Housing/Workforce Development/Education Committee 59 
develop a concise, bullet-point information sheet that EDC could distribute in support of the 60 
housing initiative. Commissioner McAnneny recommended incorporating the message "Why 61 
Housing Matters for Economic Development" into the educational materials. 62

Also discussed were different strategies that WWFH is exploring to create awareness. 64
